title: Handoff
description: One unit of delegated work, stored at <venture>/operations/handoffs/<id>.json (EE-017). It is the machine half of handoff contract v2 (operations/handoff-v2.md): who holds it, which decision rights it carries, how it is checked, and where it stands. The brief (outcome, work, context) is prose in a Markdown file beside it. schema/check-ready.mjs checks it is ready before work starts; schema/check-execution.mjs checks it against the venture's decision rights and evidence. The optional ontology block is what the membership gate reads (schema/check-nouns.mjs --package). The verdict is not stored here; it is a line in the sidecar <id>.provenance.jsonl (R-17).

governed_by.description: Decision ids this executes (EE-NNN, G-NNN, D-NNN or an ADR path)

assignment.description: Optional: the build-method assignment the work runs under, such as a MAD A-NNN, or none. MAD is a separate product, so Mentura records the reference and does not check it (EE-019, EE-038)

inputs.description: Files the work needs before it can start, from the repo root; check-ready.mjs makes sure they exist

role.description: Role id from the roles register that holds it (builder, architect and so on)

brief.description: Path to the Markdown brief, relative to this file

decision_classes.description: Decision-rights class ids the holder may use without reporting back. Anything outside them is escalated.

kind.description: conformance: an objective check run as a command, with no model and no reviewer. self-proof: the change exercised for real, with evidence attached (EE-006). review: fit to intent, judged by the named role.

check.description: The command to run, or for review the question the reviewer answers

status.description: draft until schema/check-ready.mjs passes and is recorded; then ready, in-progress, escalated or done

ready_check.description: Written by check-ready.mjs --record when every readiness item passed, before execution started

claimed_by.description: Session or run id of the holder

parent_session_id.description: Session that assigned it, for lineage

run_cap.description: Wall-clock or spend cap per run, such as 2h or $20

evidence.description: Paths to eval or check results (evidence.schema.json) that prove the done-criteria

class.description: The decision-rights class, or attempts or run-cap

lesson.description: A failure that could recur, and the check one rung higher that would catch it (prose, skill, rule, static analysis, code)

publication.description: Required when the handoff publishes (public-commitment in decision_classes or escalations): the channel and content rule in the venture's publication policy (EE-025)

ontology.description: The package's terminology. type is the one noun that decides which function the package belongs to. terms are the other nouns it uses (a noun with no function may appear in any package and never decides the type). touches lists the other functions it names. facts maps a term-engine property id to the value asserted for it and the quote that value rests on, and is read only when the type noun defines properties.

type.description: Noun id from docs/ontology.json. A package belongs to that noun's function and to no other.

terms.description: Nouns the package uses. At least one must be owned by the receiving function, or the gate rejects the package as incomplete.

touches.description: Function ids, other than the receiver, whose nouns appear in terms. A term owned by a function that is not listed here is an incomplete package.

facts.description: Term-engine property id to the asserted value and the quote it rests on (EE-095). The membership gate runs the term engine over these when the type noun lists properties.

value.description: The value the property is asserted to have. An object is the term's fact record and the engine's own checks run on it. A boolean is the assertion the engine's rule combines.

quote.description: The words in the package the value rests on.
